newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Barrick ready for Great Central bid-paper.
newsitem.headline: Barrick ready for Great Central bid-paper.

text.p: Canada's Barrick Gold Corp is expected to launch a A$3.40 per share cash takeover bid for Australian gold miner Great Central Mines Ltd, The Australian newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Market observers had said the bid, which values Great Central Mines at A$863 million, could be launched as early as Wednesday, the newspaper said.
"Barrick is preparing its Part A (takeover document) now ...it could be tomorrow, it could be three weeks," one source told The Australian on Tuesday.
Great Central executive chairman and controlling shareholder Joseph Gutnick told Reuters on Tuesday rumours of an impending bid were "just speculation".

Share market dealers attending the annual Diggers and Dealers mine conference in the gold mining centre of Kalgoorlie in Western Australia have speculated Barrick would seek to acquire Great Central in the next few days.
Speculation about a Barrick bid was first reported on July 16. Barrick said then it would not comment on the rumours.
Great Central then said in statement to the stock exchange later on July 16 it had not received or was not aware of a takeover offer from Barrick.
Great Central's shares closed up 12 cents at A$2.70 on Tuesday.
In the quarter ended June 30, 1997, Great Central yielded 106,981 ounces at an average cash cost of A$293 an ounce, company figures show.
Proved and probable reserves stand at 4.87 million ounces, the company has said.
